profile.address: 717 South Wells Street, Suite 600, Chicago, IL 60607
profile.reading: Netrality's Chicago data center occupies 717 South Wells Street, Suite 600, in the city's Financial District, Chicago, Illinois 60607. Netrality's own facility page describes 100,000 square feet of colocation space, 12,400 kilovolt diverse utility feeds, N+1 backup generator power with a 5,700 gallon fuel supply, N+1 UPS redundancy, and 600 tons of 2N chilled water cooling delivered through Kyoto and Delta Cube cooling units. A third party aggregator, DataCenterMap, independently lists this building's power capacity as 5 megawatts, with a stated power density of 125 watts per square foot for critical systems capacity, a 1.5 megawatt diesel generator, and 500 to 600 kilowatt UPS systems distributed across multiple floors. Netrality's own page lists SSAE 16 SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and PCI compliance, and states the facility hosts more than 29 on net network providers including AT&T, Verizon, Lumen, Cogent, and Zayo, along with 19 peering networks, 2 internet exchanges, and cloud connections to Lumen Cloud Connect, Megaport, and Zayo CloudLink. Netrality Data Centers is a carrier hotel and colocation operator focused on network dense, interconnection oriented buildings in secondary US markets, with other facilities in Kansas City and St. Louis already on file elsewhere in this registry. No specific year built was located for this building this session. Chicago's Financial District, known as "the Loop," has long hosted major carrier hotel buildings given the city's central role in US long haul fiber routes connecting the East and West coasts, a legacy shared with larger carrier hotel buildings elsewhere in the Loop tracked under other operators in this registry, such as 350 East Cermak. Netrality's portfolio strategy focuses on acquiring and operating this kind of legacy telecom or financial district building in secondary and network dense markets, rather than building new hyperscale campuses, positioning the company differently from wholesale operators like Digital Realty or Equinix that are also tracked elsewhere in this registry.

profile.address: 1102 Grand Boulevard, Suite 1900, Kansas City, MO 64106
profile.reading: Netrality Data Centers Kansas City, marketed as 1102 Grand, occupies the historic Bryant Building at 1102 Grand Boulevard, Suite 1900, Kansas City, Missouri 64106. Per Wikipedia's own article on the Bryant Building, the current 26 story Art Deco structure was built from 1930 to 1931 by architects Graham, Anderson, Probst and White, replacing an earlier 1891 building on the same site, and was added to the National Register of Historic Places on April 24, 1989. Per Netrality's own site and corroborating history, the building was converted to a carrier hotel data center in 2006, Netrality Data Centers acquired the property in 2012, and completed a major 14 month renovation in 2020 that upgraded power systems, added meet-me rooms and colocation cabinets, and installed three new lithium ion UPS systems on the 7th and 8th floors. Netrality's own current facility page describes 110,000 square feet of colocation space, 13,200 kilovolt diverse utility feeds, N+1 redundant backup generators with a 10,400 gallon fuel supply, a 2N UPS configuration, and 1,500 tons of N+1 condenser water cooling. The page lists SSAE 16 SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and PCI compliance, and states the facility hosts more than 120 on net network providers, 64 peering networks, 5 internet exchanges, and 11 direct cloud connections including AWS, Google Cloud, Megaport, and PacketFabric. Netrality Data Centers is a carrier hotel and colocation operator focused on network dense, interconnection oriented buildings in secondary US markets, with other facilities in Chicago and St. Louis already on file elsewhere in this registry. Kansas City sits at the crossroads of several major long haul fiber routes across the central United States, a legacy of the city's historic role as a regional telecommunications and railroad hub, which helped make the Bryant Building's conversion to a carrier hotel a natural fit for interconnection oriented tenants seeking central US latency to both coasts. Netrality's portfolio strategy focuses on acquiring and operating exactly this kind of legacy telecom or financial district building in secondary markets, rather than building new hyperscale campuses, positioning the company differently from wholesale operators like Digital Realty or Equinix that are also tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Netrality operates three colocation facilities in secondary US markets—Chicago, Kansas City, and Saint Louis—prioritizing network density and interconnection over raw power capacity in urban locations rather than suburban wholesale campuses.

The Chicago facility at 717 South Wells Street in the Financial District exemplifies this strategy. It offers 100,000 square feet of colocation space with approximately 14 megawatts of capacity and connects to 29+ on-net unique network providers across 19 peering networks, marketed as one of Chicago's most connected data centers. This dense interconnection model differs fundamentally from the large-footprint wholesale data center campuses that consume enormous power budgets. Netrality's focus on carrier hotels in downtown financial districts suggests a market segment serving customers who value network path diversity and low-latency peering over massive compute density in any single location.

Ownership history shows possible transition from CIM Group in 2018 to Macquarie Asset Management per current materials, though this registry could not fully reconcile the timeline. Current power consumption and square footage data for Kansas City and Saint Louis facilities remain unmeasured. Saint Louis itself lists two separately addressed Netrality facilities that appear complementary rather than redundant, indicating the operator's strategy emphasizes geographic distribution of interconnection points within secondary markets rather than consolidation into single large buildings.
